title: Surviving the Night
summary: Put the device you use for porn out of reach before you sleep.
label: TONIGHT'S TASK
intro: Set up tonight before you get tired. Use the option that matches where you sleep.

bullets.head: Own bedroom
bullets.body: Set the alarm now. Charge the phone outside the room. Put a laptop or tablet in a closed bag, drawer, or cupboard away from the bed.

bullets.head: Shared room
bullets.body: Put the device in a bag, locker, desk drawer, or fixed charging spot that you cannot reach while lying down.

bullets.head: Studio, sofa bed, or temporary space
bullets.body: Put the device at the farthest practical point from where you sleep: a kitchen counter, shelf, zipped bag, or other fixed place.

bullets.head: Phone needed as an alarm
bullets.body: Set the alarm first. Put the phone across the room or outside it. Turn off non-essential notifications before you put it down.

done: The task is done when you cannot reach the device you usually use for porn from bed without standing up and moving.

title: A New Start
summary: Clean the space you use most and remove easy porn cues.
label: TODAY'S TASK
intro: Set a 20-minute timer. Clean only the physical and digital space you control. Stop when the timer rings.

bullets.head: Own room
bullets.body: Make the bed. Open the curtains or blinds. Put dirty clothes in a hamper or bag. Throw out rubbish. Clear the floor, desk, and bedside surface.

bullets.head: Shared room
bullets.body: Clean your bed, desk, shelf, drawer, bag, and devices. Leave the other person's things alone.

bullets.head: No fixed room
bullets.body: Pick one area you use every day - a desk, shelf, bag, bedside corner, or your side of a shared space - and clean that.

bullets.head: Digital
bullets.body: Delete saved porn. Close old tabs. Log out of accounts you use to find it. Remove bookmarks and shortcuts. Move risky apps off the home screen.

done: The task is done when the timer rings and the area you use most is cleaner, with fewer porn-related files, accounts, or objects within easy reach.

title: Get Outside
summary: Spend 20 minutes away from your usual relapse setting.
label: TODAY'S TASK
intro: Spend 20 minutes away from the place where you are most likely to relapse.

bullets.head: Good weather
bullets.body: Walk around the block, sit in a park, get a drink, run an errand, or take a route that keeps you moving.

bullets.head: Bad weather
bullets.body: Use a library, cafe, gym, lobby, shopping centre, covered walkway, or another shared indoor place.

bullets.head: Cannot leave home
bullets.body: Move to the least isolated part of the home. Open the curtains. Sit near other people if possible. Use a window, balcony, or doorway for fresh air.

bullets.head: Urge already strong
bullets.body: Close the tab or app first. Leave the room before deciding anything else. Take the phone only if you need it for safety or directions.

done: The task is done when you have spent 20 minutes away from the usual relapse setting without continuing the same sexual or endless scrolling elsewhere.

title: Fix Your Sleep
summary: Set tomorrow's alarm and decide when and where your phone goes away tonight.
label: TODAY'S TASK
intro: Set tomorrow's alarm now. Then choose the exact time and place where the phone goes away tonight.

bullets.head: Normal school or work hours
bullets.body: Pick a realistic wake time. Put the phone away 30-60 minutes before you intend to sleep.

bullets.head: Late shift or irregular hours
bullets.body: Use the same sequence around your actual schedule: finish work, wind down, phone away, sleep, then wake when your schedule requires.

bullets.head: Phone is your alarm
bullets.body: Set the alarm before the cutoff. Put the phone across the room or outside the bedroom.

bullets.head: Shared room
bullets.body: Use a bag, drawer, locker, or fixed charging spot away from the bed so the device has the same place every night.

done: The task is done when the alarm is set, the phone cutoff has a clock time, and the phone has a fixed place for the night.

title: What Replaces Porn?
summary: Spend 20 minutes learning something new.
label: TODAY'S TASK
intro: Set a 20-minute timer and learn one new thing. Pick the topic within two minutes, then start.

bullets.head: Computers
bullets.body: Follow one short coding tutorial, learn one command, build one tiny component, or understand how one tool works.

bullets.head: Practical skill
bullets.body: Learn a Rubik's Cube algorithm, guitar chord, cooking technique, knot, repair, card trick, or exercise movement.

bullets.head: Ideas
bullets.body: Read about one historical event, scientific idea, philosophical argument, language rule, or question you have wondered about.

bullets.head: No idea what to choose
bullets.body: Open a book, course, or tutorial you already own and learn the next small section. Do not spend the session searching for the perfect topic.

done: The task is done when the 20 minutes ends and you can explain, demonstrate, or use one thing you could not before the session.

title: Isolation
summary: Spend at least 10 minutes talking with or being around another person.
label: TODAY'S TASK
intro: Spend at least 10 minutes talking with or spending time with another person today. You do not need to mention recovery.

bullets.head: Someone nearby
bullets.body: Eat with them, walk with them, sit in a common area, attend a class or club, or stay for a conversation instead of leaving immediately.

bullets.head: People far away
bullets.body: Call someone. If you text, ask a question, suggest a call, or make a plan that gives them something to answer.

bullets.head: No close person comes to mind
bullets.body: Go to a repeated social setting such as a sports session, class, club, study space, workplace common area, or regular cafe.

bullets.head: Busy day
bullets.body: Use a short window: eat lunch with someone, walk with a colleague, or make a 10-minute call.

done: The task is done when you have spent at least 10 minutes talking with someone or doing something together.

title: One Week In
summary: Reward yourself for finishing your first week.
label: TODAY'S TASK
intro: Do something you enjoy because you finished Week 1. It does not have to be productive.

bullets.head: Food
bullets.body: Get ice cream, a favourite snack, coffee, a meal you like, or cook something you normally save for a good day.

bullets.head: Activity
bullets.body: Watch a film, play a game, go somewhere you like, take a long bath, visit a shop, read for pleasure, or spend time on a hobby.

bullets.head: Social
bullets.body: Go for food with someone, meet a friend, play sport, or do something fun together.

bullets.head: Money is tight
bullets.body: Use a free reward: a long walk, favourite film at home, game with friends, cooking something good, or an uninterrupted hour on something you enjoy.

done: The task is done when you have taken the reward. There is no extra recovery assignment today.

title: More Than a Streak
summary: Notice three ways your behaviour has changed and repeat one today.
label: TODAY'S TASK
intro: Open your Vici history or think back over the last seven days. Write down three things that have changed.

bullets.head: Before or during an urge
bullets.body: Write about one thing you handle differently now, such as noticing it earlier, leaving the room, putting the phone down, or opening Urge Surfing.

bullets.head: After a bad moment
bullets.body: Write about anything you do differently afterwards. If nothing has changed yet, say so.

bullets.head: Outside porn
bullets.body: Write about anything that has improved this week, such as sleep, work, exercise, relationships, or a hobby.

done: The task is done when the three changes are written and you have repeated one of them.
extra: Pick one improvement you wrote down and repeat that behaviour today. If nothing has improved yet, pick one behaviour you want to change and do it once today.

title: After a Relapse
summary: Review what happened after your last relapse and plan how to stop the next part sooner.
label: TODAY'S TASK
intro: Open Notes. Think about your most recent relapse. If you have never relapsed, use the closest call you remember.

bullets.head: What happened next
bullets.body: Write what you did during the first 30 minutes afterwards. Be literal: kept watching, stayed in bed, kept scrolling, skipped sleep, cancelled plans, or whatever happened.

bullets.head: First chance to stop
bullets.body: Write the earliest point when you could have stopped the next part from happening.

bullets.head: Next time
bullets.body: Write three actions you can start within five minutes. For example: close every porn tab, put the phone in the kitchen, take a shower, then return to breakfast, work, class, or sleep.

bullets.head: Device
bullets.body: Write exactly where the phone or laptop will go during those first five minutes.

done: The task is done when the note tells you what happened, where you could have stopped the next step, and what you will do next time.

title: The All-or-Nothing Trap
summary: Practise a four-step plan for stopping one relapse from turning into another.
label: TODAY'S TASK
intro: Write four steps you will take after a relapse so it does not turn into another one. Then practise the steps once today.

bullets.head: Step 1 -- End the episode
bullets.body: Close every porn tab or file and put the device in the place you chose for it.

bullets.head: Step 2 -- Leave
bullets.body: Go to one exact place for 20 minutes: a park bench, cafe, library, lobby, common room, convenience store, or a fixed walking route.

bullets.head: Step 3 -- Keep the phone out of it
bullets.body: Leave it behind if that is safe. If you need it for directions or calls, keep it zipped away and do not open feeds or the browser.

bullets.head: Step 4 -- Continue the day
bullets.body: Write what comes next: eat, shower, go to class, finish a work block, see someone, or go to sleep.

done: The task is done when the four steps are written and you have physically tested the route.
extra: Write the four steps in Notes and walk the route once today. The relapse is already over. These steps are there to stop it becoming an excuse for another relapse or for abandoning the rest of the day.

title: Progress Isn't Linear
summary: Compare this week with before Vici and change the area that still causes the most trouble.
label: TODAY'S TASK
intro: Compare the last seven days with the period just before you started Vici. Use the app if it has the data; otherwise use what you can remember. Write a short comparison in three areas:

bullets.head: Urges
bullets.body: Compare their frequency or strength, how early you notice them, or what you do when they appear.

bullets.head: After a bad moment
bullets.body: Compare how long it takes you to get back to the rest of your day and what you do afterwards.

bullets.head: Routine
bullets.body: Compare sleep, phone location, time alone, exercise, work, or contact with other people.

done: The task is done when the three comparisons are written and you have started the change for the next seven days.
extra: An area can be unchanged or worse. Pick the one that still causes the most trouble and decide what you will change for the next seven days. Start that change today.

title: Identity
summary: Choose one behaviour you want to repeat for the next week and prepare for it today.
label: TODAY'S TASK
intro: Pick one behaviour you want to repeat for the next seven days. Write down when it happens and what you will do.

bullets.head: Phone
bullets.body: Decide where your phone will stay when you go to bed.

bullets.head: Work or study
bullets.body: Decide what work happens before you open feeds.

bullets.head: Health
bullets.body: Decide which days and times you will train, walk, or exercise.

bullets.head: People
bullets.body: Decide who you will call or meet and when.

bullets.head: Recovery
bullets.body: Decide what you will do first if you notice yourself starting to search for porn.

done: The task is done when the rule is written, anything it needs has been prepared, and the first repetition has happened or is scheduled.
extra: Prepare for the rule now: move the charger, create the calendar event, lay out the equipment, or place the shortcut where you need it. Do the first repetition today if the timing allows.

title: Values, Not Shame
summary: Spend 20 minutes on something you care about that porn has been taking time from.
label: TODAY'S TASK
intro: Write down something you care about that has been getting less time than you want. Spend 20 minutes on it today.

bullets.head: People
bullets.body: Call, meet, help, or spend time with someone without doing something else at the same time.

bullets.head: Work or study
bullets.body: Work for 20 minutes on something you already need to do, with the phone out of reach.

bullets.head: Health
bullets.body: Walk, train, cook, stretch, or set up sleep for tonight.

bullets.head: Faith, community, creativity, or something else
bullets.body: Do one activity that belongs to it for 20 minutes.

done: The task is done when you have written the answer and spent 20 minutes on it.

title: Keep Going
summary: Make a simple plan for how you will continue after missed days, relapse, or low motivation.
label: TODAY'S TASK
intro: Open Notes and make a short continuation plan for the days when you feel like abandoning everything.

bullets.head: Missing a day
bullets.body: Write when and how you will resume. Do not plan to restart from Day 1 or catch up several lessons at once.

bullets.head: Relapsing
bullets.body: Write what you will do afterwards. Include the Lesson 10 steps and one ordinary part of the day that still happens, such as the next meal, class, work block, training session, or bedtime.

bullets.head: Losing motivation
bullets.body: Write one thing you will still do, such as keeping the phone out of bed, going outside, going to bed on time, or contacting someone.

extra: Pin the note somewhere easy to find. The task is done when you know what you will do in all three situations without waiting to feel motivated.

title: The Life of an Urge
summary: Keep your phone away for 10 minutes and rate how much you want to check it.
label: TODAY'S TASK
intro: Put your phone in another room for 10 minutes and track how much you want to check it.

bullets.head: Start
bullets.body: On paper, write 0 minutes and rate the urge to check the phone from 0 to 10.

bullets.head: Five minutes
bullets.body: Write the number again. Leave the phone where it is.

bullets.head: Ten minutes
bullets.body: Write the final number.

done: The task is done when the phone has stayed out of reach for 10 minutes and you have written all three ratings.

title: What's the Urge Really For?
summary: Look at the circumstances around your most recent strong urge.
label: TODAY'S TASK
intro: Use your most recent strong urge, relapse, or close call. Write five facts about what was happening around it.

bullets.head: Place and time
bullets.body: Where were you, and roughly what time was it?

bullets.head: Previous 30 minutes
bullets.body: What had you been doing immediately beforehand?

bullets.head: Body
bullets.body: Were you hungry, tired, physically aroused, restless, or none of those?

bullets.head: Mood
bullets.body: Which word fits best: bored, stressed, lonely, angry, anxious, sad, calm, or something else?

bullets.head: What you were avoiding
bullets.body: Was there a task, message, conversation, or responsibility you were putting off? If not, write that there was nothing obvious.

done: The task is done when all five facts are written. If you do not know why the urge happened, leave it at that.

title: Move First
summary: Practise leaving the place where you are most likely to relapse.
label: TODAY'S TASK
intro: Practise the exact movement you will use to leave your most common relapse setting. Do the full sequence once now.

bullets.head: Bedroom
bullets.body: Lock the phone, put both feet on the floor, stand up, put the phone in its charging place, and leave the room for two minutes.

bullets.head: Desk
bullets.body: Close the browser, lock the screen, stand up, get water, and move to a shared or public seat.

bullets.head: Bathroom
bullets.body: Put the phone outside before entering. Walk in, then walk back out without taking it with you.

bullets.head: Hotel, dorm, or temporary room
bullets.body: Put the phone in a bag, drawer, or safe if available, then walk to the lobby, corridor, common room, or another public area.

done: The task is done when you have physically performed the whole exit sequence once.

title: Redirection
summary: Prepare four easy things you can do instead of staying on a screen.
label: TODAY'S TASK
intro: Set up four things you can start in under a minute when you need to get off a screen.

bullets.head: Two-minute option
bullets.body: Leave something obvious ready: tea, a small chore, shower items, a stretching mat, or anything else you can start at once.

bullets.head: Leave-the-room option
bullets.body: Put shoes, keys, coat, umbrella, or a gym bag where you can grab them quickly.

bullets.head: Something that holds your attention
bullets.body: Put a book on the desk, leave the instrument out, open the project file, or prepare another hobby.

bullets.head: Person
bullets.body: Favourite or pin one person you can call or message.

done: The task is done when all four options can be started in under a minute.

title: HALT
summary: Check whether you are hungry, angry, lonely, or tired and deal with any that apply.
label: TODAY'S TASK
intro: Run a HALT check now. Open Notes and write four lines: Hungry, Angry, Lonely, Tired. Put "yes" or "no" beside each one.

bullets.head: Hungry = yes
bullets.body: Eat a proper meal or snack and drink water.

bullets.head: Angry = yes
bullets.body: Take a 10-minute walk, shower, exercise, or step away from the argument if it is safe to do so.

bullets.head: Lonely = yes
bullets.body: Call someone, send a message that starts a conversation, or sit in a shared place for 10 minutes.

bullets.head: Tired = yes
bullets.body: Set tonight's alarm and phone cutoff now. If you can safely rest, take a short planned rest.

done: The task is done when all four answers are written and you have done something about every "yes."

title: Urge Surfing
summary: Practise urge surfing for five minutes using the urge to check your phone.
label: TODAY'S TASK
intro: Put your phone out of reach for five minutes and use the urge to check it to practise urge surfing.

bullets.head: Start
bullets.body: Set a five-minute timer on another device, watch, or kitchen timer if you have one.

bullets.head: Notice the body
bullets.body: Write where you feel the urge to reach for the phone: hands, chest, jaw, stomach, restlessness, or somewhere else.

bullets.head: Stay with it
bullets.body: Do not check the phone. If the sensation changes, add a short note.

done: The task is done when five minutes have passed without checking the phone and you have written at least one physical sensation.

title: Masturbation
summary: Set a two-week masturbation rule based on whether it tends to lead you back to porn.
label: TODAY'S TASK
intro: Decide how you want to handle masturbation for the next two weeks. Keep the decision about porn separate from a general judgment about masturbation. Only make the rule stricter if masturbation tends to lead you back to porn.

bullets.head: If masturbation does not usually lead you to porn
bullets.body: Keep it allowed if that fits your values. Porn, sexual browsing, and porn-capable devices stay out of it.

bullets.head: If masturbation often leads directly to porn
bullets.body: Either take a two-week break or keep the phone and laptop completely outside the room. Choose the option you are more likely to follow.

bullets.head: If you are not sure
bullets.body: Do not ban it by default. Keep screens out of it and, if masturbation happens during the next two weeks, briefly note whether porn was involved, whether a porn-capable device was in the room, and whether it led to sexual searching afterwards.

bullets.head: If you choose not to masturbate for personal or religious reasons
bullets.body: Write that boundary plainly and leave it there. You do not need a second reason.

extra: Move the devices to the place your rule requires. The task is done when the rule is written and the devices are where you said they would be.

title: The Reward System
summary: Remove one set of cues that regularly puts sexual content in front of you.
label: TODAY'S TASK
intro: Set a 10-minute timer and remove one group of cues that regularly puts sexual content in front of you.

bullets.head: Feeds
bullets.body: Unfollow, mute, or block sexualised accounts and recommendation pages.

bullets.head: Browser
bullets.body: Delete saved links, old tabs, bookmarks, and autofill entries that lead back to porn.

bullets.head: Apps
bullets.body: Delete the app, log out, or move it off the home screen if it repeatedly starts the same sequence.

bullets.head: Room
bullets.body: Move the charger, laptop, or other device away from the place where you usually use porn.

done: The task is done when the timer ends and at least one recurring cue is harder to reach or no longer appears automatically.

title: The Control Center
summary: Put Vici Urge Surfing one tap away and give your phone a fixed place for tonight.
label: TODAY'S TASK
intro: Put Vici's Urge Surfing tool where you can open it in one tap.

bullets.head: Home Screen
bullets.body: Add the Vici Urge Surfing widget or shortcut somewhere you can see without opening a folder.

bullets.head: Lock Screen
bullets.body: If you would rather use the Lock Screen, add the shortcut there instead.

bullets.head: Check it
bullets.body: Tap it once and make sure it opens Urge Surfing directly.

bullets.head: Tonight
bullets.body: Move the charger to the place where the phone will stay while you sleep.

done: The task is done when Urge Surfing opens in one tap and the phone has a fixed place for tonight.

title: Hungry and Tired
summary: Eat, drink, and prepare for sleep before the risky part of the day.
label: TODAY'S TASK
intro: Set up the physical conditions for tonight before the risky part of the day begins.

bullets.head: Food
bullets.body: Decide what your next proper meal is and eat it before you become very hungry.

bullets.head: Water
bullets.body: Fill a bottle or glass now and keep it somewhere you will drink from it.

bullets.head: Sleep
bullets.body: Set the next alarm and decide the exact time your phone leaves the bed or sleeping area.

bullets.head: Shift work
bullets.body: Use the same steps before the sleep period that fits your schedule; it does not have to happen at night.

done: The task is done when the meal is handled, water is ready, and the next sleep period has an alarm and a phone cutoff.

title: Angry and Lonely
summary: Compare how anger and loneliness affect you and practise one response.
label: TODAY'S TASK
intro: Use one past example of anger and one past example of loneliness. Write three short lines for each so you can tell the two apart when they happen again.

bullets.head: Anger
bullets.body: Write what happened, one physical sign you remember in your body, and the first safe action that would have helped: walk, train, cool down, delay the message, or talk to someone.

bullets.head: Loneliness
bullets.body: Write what was happening, what you did next, and what could have put you around another person: call someone, eat with people, work in a shared place, or make a plan.

done: The task is done when both examples are written and you have practised one of the actions.
extra: Pick whichever causes more trouble for you and practise what you would do today. If you are neither angry nor lonely today, practise while calm so the action is familiar next time.

title: The Pull of Novelty
summary: Spend 15 minutes on one thing without switching to something newer.
label: TODAY'S TASK
intro: Run a 15-minute no-switching exercise and count how often you want to abandon the thing in front of you for something newer.

bullets.head: Choose one thing with a fixed end
bullets.body: one article, one chapter, one tutorial, one document, one piece of music, or another single item.

bullets.head: Close every unrelated tab or app. Turn off autoplay if it applies.
Put a sheet of paper beside you. Every time you want to switch tabs, check another app, search for something new, or skip ahead for novelty, make one tally mark and stay with the original item.

done: The task is done when the 15 minutes are over and you have a tally count.
extra: At the end, write the number of tally marks. Do not aim for zero; the count only shows how often you wanted to switch.

title: Change Your State
summary: Compare your physical arousal before and after movement and slower breathing.
label: TODAY'S TASK
intro: See what six minutes of movement and slower breathing do to your physical arousal, even if you do not have an urge today.

bullets.head: Before
bullets.body: Sit still for 30 seconds and rate your physical activation from 0 to 10. Base the number on breathing, muscle tension, restlessness, and heart rate, not your mood.

bullets.head: Move
bullets.body: Spend two minutes walking briskly, doing gentle body-weight movement, or moving within your normal physical limits.

bullets.head: Slow down
bullets.body: Sit or stand comfortably and breathe slowly for three minutes. Try about four seconds in and six seconds out. If that feels uncomfortable, breathe normally and lengthen the exhale a little.

bullets.head: After
bullets.body: Rate it from 0 to 10 again and write what changed, if anything.

done: The task is done when both ratings and the one-sentence observation are written.

title: Autopilot
summary: Change the first action that usually starts your porn routine.
label: TODAY'S TASK
intro: Look at the first action that usually starts the sequence: taking the phone into bed, opening a certain app, moving to a private room, or beginning a search. Change that action today.

bullets.head: Phone goes to bed
bullets.body: Move the charger outside the bed area.

bullets.head: Phone goes to the bathroom
bullets.body: Put a fixed shelf, bag, or charging place outside the bathroom.

bullets.head: One app starts it
bullets.body: Delete it, log out, or remove it from the Home Screen.

bullets.head: You move to a private room
bullets.body: Leave the phone outside that room or use a shared place for what you were about to do.

done: The task is done when that first step is harder to repeat in the same way.

title: The Scale
summary: Plan one high-risk two-hour block before it arrives.
label: TODAY'S TASK
intro: Open your calendar. Pick a two-hour block in the next three days when you are likely to be alone, tired, bored, or unstructured. Decide in advance where you will be, what you will do, and where the phone will stay.

bullets.head: Place
bullets.body: Write where you will be: library, gym, cafe, common room, kitchen, friend's place, class, or another shared setting.

bullets.head: Activity
bullets.body: Write exactly what you will do during the block.

bullets.head: Phone rule
bullets.body: Write where the phone will stay. If you expect an urge, make sure the Vici Urge Surfing shortcut or widget is already on your Home Screen or Lock Screen.

bullets.head: If your schedule changes constantly
bullets.body: Use tonight or the next evening you expect to be free.

done: The task is done when the two-hour block is on the calendar with a place, activity, and phone rule.

title: The "Benefits" of Porn
summary: Spend 20 minutes meeting the need that usually makes porn appealing in another way.
label: TODAY'S TASK
intro: Choose the reason porn is most appealing to you in the moment. Then spend 20 minutes getting the same thing another way.

bullets.head: Relief
bullets.body: Shower, walk, exercise, lie down without the phone, or finish the task that is hanging over you.

bullets.head: Stimulation
bullets.body: Go somewhere different, train, cook, play a game with a clear end, or learn something new.

bullets.head: Comfort
bullets.body: Eat, make tea, rest, call someone, or watch a film or episode you chose beforehand without opening a feed afterwards.

bullets.head: Sexual release
bullets.body: Follow the masturbation rule you set in Lesson 21 and keep porn-capable devices out of it.

done: The task is done when you have spent 20 minutes on the alternative without opening porn.

title: The Hidden Reward
summary: Spend 15 minutes starting something you have been avoiding.
label: TODAY'S TASK
intro: Pick one task, message, decision, or piece of admin you have been avoiding. Set a 15-minute timer and start it now.

bullets.head: Work or study
bullets.body: Open the file and do the first visible piece.

bullets.head: Message
bullets.body: Send the reply or ask the question.

bullets.head: Admin
bullets.body: Open the form, book the appointment, pay the bill, or gather the required documents.

bullets.head: Decision
bullets.body: Write the two or three options you have and do the next thing needed to decide.

done: The task is done when the 15-minute timer ends and you have done something you can point to.

title: The Short-Term Cost
summary: Write down what a late relapse costs tomorrow morning and prepare that morning now.
label: TODAY'S TASK
intro: Open Notes. Write three things a late relapse tends to cost you the next morning. Then set the alarm, first activity, and phone location for tomorrow.

bullets.head: Write three costs you have felt the next morning
bullets.body: lost sleep, missing class, being late, skipping breakfast, cancelling training, or losing the first hour of work.

bullets.head: Set the alarm
bullets.body: Choose the time you need to get up.

bullets.head: Set the first activity
bullets.body: Put breakfast, class, work, a walk, gym, or another morning activity on the calendar.

bullets.head: Move the phone
bullets.body: Put the charger where the phone will stay tonight.

done: The task is done when the three costs are written and tomorrow has an alarm, a first activity, and a phone location.

title: The Long-Term Cost
summary: Spend 30 minutes on something you want to be better a year from now.
label: TODAY'S TASK
intro: Pick something you want to improve over the next year and work on it for 30 minutes today.

bullets.head: Study or work
bullets.body: Work on a course, application, portfolio, project, or skill you are already doing.

bullets.head: Health
bullets.body: Train, walk, cook, book an appointment, or prepare for an earlier night.

bullets.head: Relationship
bullets.body: Call, meet, repair, or make a plan with someone.

bullets.head: Project or hobby
bullets.body: Build, practise, write, draw, code, cook, or make something for 30 minutes.

done: The task is done after 30 minutes on the thing you chose.

title: Tipping the Scale
summary: Make porn harder to reach by removing one saved route and moving one device.
label: TODAY'S TASK
intro: Make two changes before your usual high-risk time: remove one saved shortcut back to porn and move one device.

bullets.head: Saved shortcut
bullets.body: Delete one porn bookmark, saved file, stored login, open tab group, secondary account, or another saved way you have used to get there quickly.

bullets.head: Feed or account
bullets.body: If recommendations are the problem, unfollow, mute, or log out of the account that keeps leading you there.

bullets.head: Physical change
bullets.body: Move the phone charger, laptop, or tablet away from the bed, bathroom, or private place where you usually use porn.

bullets.head: Nothing obvious to delete
bullets.body: Skip the digital step and make a second physical change instead, such as putting the laptop in a bag or moving the tablet to a shared room.

done: The task is done when both routes take more effort to reach than they did this morning.

title: Repairing the Scale
summary: Schedule four sessions of something you want more of in your week.
label: TODAY'S TASK
intro: Choose one activity you want in your week. Schedule the next four sessions now.

bullets.head: Social
bullets.body: Put a weekly meal, call, game, club, or visit on the calendar and send the first invitation.

bullets.head: Exercise
bullets.body: Schedule the next four workouts, classes, walks, or training sessions.

bullets.head: Skill or hobby
bullets.body: Block the time and prepare what you need for the first session.

bullets.head: Project
bullets.body: Put four work blocks on the calendar and open the project today for at least 10 minutes.

done: The task is done when all four sessions are on the calendar and you have started the first one or sent whatever message is needed.

title: What is Willpower?
summary: Spend 15 minutes staying with one task even when you want to switch away.
label: TODAY'S TASK
intro: Set a 15-minute timer and pick a task you have been putting off. Put your phone out of reach and work only on that task until the timer ends.

bullets.head: Keep it small
bullets.body: answer one email, wash the dishes, read a required page, organise your bag, pay a bill, clean one surface, or complete one small piece of work.

bullets.head: If the task is large
bullets.body: choose the first part that can be done in 15 minutes. Do not use the time to plan the whole project.

bullets.head: If you want to check your phone or switch tasks
bullets.body: notice the impulse and return to what you chose until the timer ends.

done: The task is done when you have stayed with the chosen task for the full 15 minutes.

title: Train Your Response
summary: Practise your urge-exit sequence three times.
label: TODAY'S TASK
intro: Do three repetitions of your physical urge-exit sequence now.

bullets.head: Each repetition
bullets.body: Put the phone down, lock the screen, stand up, leave the room, walk to the place you chose, then return.

bullets.head: Practise where it usually happens
bullets.body: the bed, desk, bathroom entrance, or another place where the sequence tends to start.

bullets.head: Keep each repetition short
bullets.body: Practise the first movement only. Come back after a minute or two.

done: The task is done when you have performed the same exit sequence three times.

title: What Discipline Isn't
summary: Finish one necessary task without turning it into a punishment or test.
label: TODAY'S TASK
intro: Pick a necessary task that takes 20 minutes or less and finish it without rushing or turning it into a test of discipline.

bullets.head: Work or study
bullets.body: Answer the email, finish one problem set section, read the assigned pages, or submit the form.

bullets.head: Home
bullets.body: Do the dishes, laundry, rubbish, shopping list, or one cleaning job.

bullets.head: Health
bullets.body: Do the planned short workout, cook the meal, or book the appointment.

bullets.head: Stop when finished
bullets.body: Do not add a punishment workout, extra hour, or impossible standard because you think the task was too easy.

done: The task is done when the chosen task is finished. Nothing extra is required.

title: What Discipline Is
summary: Practise starting, staying with, returning to, and stopping a task on time.
label: TODAY'S TASK
intro: Use a task you already need to do to practise starting, staying with it, coming back after a break, and stopping on time.

bullets.head: Start
bullets.body: Begin within two minutes of opening this task.

bullets.head: Stay
bullets.body: Work for 10 minutes without switching to another app or job.

bullets.head: Return
bullets.body: At the 10-minute mark, stand up for one minute, then come back and work for another five minutes.

bullets.head: Stop
bullets.body: When the 15 minutes are over, stop even if you could keep going.

done: The task is done when you have completed the full 15-minute run.

title: Thoughts and Feelings
summary: Write down a thought that usually comes before porn and practise what you want to do instead.
label: TODAY'S TASK
intro: Open Notes. Write the exact sentence you tend to tell yourself right before you keep scrolling, start searching, or open porn.

bullets.head: Use your own words
bullets.body: It might be something like 'only for a minute,' 'I already messed up today,' or 'I am too tired to care.'

bullets.head: Under it, write what you want to do when that thought shows up
bullets.body: lock the phone, stand up, leave the room, open Vici Urge Surfing, or return to what you were meant to be doing.

done: The task is done when the thought and the action are written and you have practised the action once.

title: Choose Your Action
summary: Write three simple rules for situations that have caught you before and make one easier to follow.
label: TODAY'S TASK
intro: Write three rules for situations that have caught you before. Keep each rule to one sentence.

bullets.head: Phone in bed
bullets.body: If the phone reaches the bed, put it back in the charging place before lying down.

bullets.head: Sexual content
bullets.body: If you open sexual content, close it, lock the phone, and stand up.

bullets.head: Searching for porn
bullets.body: If you notice yourself starting to search, open Vici Urge Surfing before doing anything else.

bullets.head: Make one rule easier to follow
bullets.body: Move the charger or add the Vici Urge Surfing shortcut or widget to the Home Screen or Lock Screen.

done: The task is done when the three rules are written and you have changed the phone or room to make one of them easier to follow.

title: Damage Control
summary: Decide the three things you will still do on a bad day.
label: TODAY'S TASK
intro: Write three things you will still do on a bad day. Keep the list small.

bullets.head: Food
bullets.body: Decide what counts as enough for you, such as two proper meals.

bullets.head: Phone
bullets.body: Keep it out of bed.

bullets.head: Sleep
bullets.body: Set an alarm and start trying to sleep within an hour of the time you planned.

bullets.head: Save the list somewhere easy to find, such as a pinned note or a card near the bed.

done: The task is done when the three rules are saved somewhere you can reach on a bad day.

title: Relapse Isn't The End
summary: Write down what the next 24 hours should look like after a relapse.
label: TODAY'S TASK
intro: Write down what the next 24 hours should look like after a relapse. Keep the ordinary parts of the day in it.
Cover these five things:

bullets.head: The next proper meal you will still eat.
The next responsibility you will still keep.
One person you will stay in contact with instead of disappearing.
Where your phone will go at bedtime.
What you will start with tomorrow morning.

done: The task is done when all five parts are written and tomorrow morning has been prepared.
extra: If you have relapsed recently, use today. If you have not, write this for the next time it happens. Prepare tomorrow morning now by laying out what you need, setting the alarm, or putting the first task on your desk.

title: Learn From the Relapse
summary: Reconstruct your last relapse and change the earliest step you can control.
label: TODAY'S TASK
intro: Use your most recent relapse and write what happened in order.

bullets.head: Two hours before
bullets.body: Where were you and what were you doing?

bullets.head: Device
bullets.body: What were you using?

bullets.head: First cue
bullets.body: What was the first sexual account, search, post, thought, or other cue you followed?

bullets.head: First move toward porn
bullets.body: What did you do next: take the phone to bed, open an app, go somewhere private, or start searching?

bullets.head: Just before the relapse
bullets.body: What happened immediately beforehand?

bullets.head: Earliest change
bullets.body: Which earlier step could you realistically change next time?

bullets.head: Change it today
bullets.body: Move the charger, delete or log out of the account, remove the shortcut, or change the place named above.

done: The task is done when the events are written in order and the earliest change has been made today.

title: Don't Punish Yourself
summary: Write and save a plan for the first hour after a relapse.
label: TODAY'S TASK
intro: Write what you will do during the first hour after a relapse. Use the timings below.

bullets.head: First 5 minutes
bullets.body: Close every porn tab. Lock the device. Put it in its charging place or another room. Leave the place where the relapse happened.

bullets.head: Next 20 minutes
bullets.body: Shower, eat, drink water, or take a short walk. Pick one.

bullets.head: Rest of the hour
bullets.body: Go back to whatever was next before the relapse. If it is late, go to sleep. If it is daytime, return to class, work, food, exercise, or another plan.

bullets.head: Save the three time blocks in a pinned note.

done: The task is done when the note is written and pinned.

title: Rough Days
summary: Reduce a rough day to three things that still need to happen.
label: TODAY'S TASK
intro: Cut the rest of today down to three things. Write them down, then start the first one.

bullets.head: One thing that cannot wait
bullets.body: A class, shift, email, assignment, appointment, or piece of admin.

bullets.head: One thing for your body
bullets.body: A proper meal, shower, medication you normally take, or a 20-minute walk.

bullets.head: Tonight
bullets.body: Set the alarm and decide where the phone will stay while you sleep.

bullets.head: Cross out optional catch-up work, extra training, and non-urgent errands for today.

done: The task is done when the list has three items and the first one has been started.

title: When Life Gets Hard
summary: Decide what you will keep doing through several bad days and tell someone you may contact them.
label: TODAY'S TASK
intro: Decide what you will still do if you have three bad days in a row. Then tell one person you may contact them.

bullets.head: Pick two basics you will do every day
bullets.body: phone outside bed, two proper meals, the same wake time, or 20 minutes outside.

bullets.head: Pick one place for the evening
bullets.body: library, common room, gym, cafe, family area, or another shared place.

bullets.head: Pick one person you can call or message.
Send them a short message asking whether it is okay to call or message if you have a rough few days. Use your own words.

done: The task is done when the three-day note is written and the message has been sent.

title: Face What You're Avoiding
summary: Spend 15 minutes on the first part of something you have been avoiding.
label: TODAY'S TASK
intro: Pick something you have been avoiding. Write down the first part you can do without having to finish the whole problem, then work on it for 15 minutes.

bullets.head: Work or study
bullets.body: Open the file and produce one paragraph, calculation, outline, or other visible piece of work.

bullets.head: Message
bullets.body: Read it once and send the reply or the question you need answered.

bullets.head: Money or admin
bullets.body: Open the account, pay one bill, gather the document, submit the form, or make the call.

bullets.head: Conversation
bullets.body: If it is safe, send a message and ask when they can talk.

bullets.head: Health
bullets.body: Book the appointment, write the symptoms you need to describe, or prepare what you need for the visit.

extra: Stop after 15 minutes if you want. The task is done when you have done one part of the thing you were avoiding.

title: Don't Wait for Tomorrow
summary: Start something today that you were going to leave until tomorrow.
label: TODAY'S TASK
intro: Set a 10-minute timer and start something you were going to leave until tomorrow.

bullets.head: Work or study
bullets.body: Open the file and start.

bullets.head: Home
bullets.body: Wash the dishes, clear one surface, take out rubbish, or start the laundry.

bullets.head: Body
bullets.body: Walk, stretch, shower, cook, or prepare the next meal.

bullets.head: People
bullets.body: Send the message, make the call, or arrange the plan.

done: The task is done when the 10-minute timer ends. You may stop then.

title: Boredom
summary: Spend 10 minutes without filling boredom with new content.
label: TODAY'S TASK
intro: Set a 10-minute timer and spend the whole 10 minutes without opening anything new: no feed, video, message thread, article, podcast, or porn.

bullets.head: Put away
bullets.body: Phone, laptop, music, podcast, video, porn, and social feeds.

bullets.head: Do
bullets.body: Sit, stand outside, make tea, look out the window, walk slowly, or simply stay still.

bullets.head: Work or commute
bullets.body: Use the 10 minutes as a break: walk, stretch, get water, or look around without opening a feed.

done: The task is done when the timer ends and you have not opened something else to fill the time.

title: Escaping Boredom
summary: Take a 20-minute walk without using your phone.
label: TODAY'S TASK
intro: Take a 20-minute walk without using your phone.

bullets.head: Leave it behind
bullets.body: If it is safe, leave the phone at home, in your room, or in a locker.

bullets.head: Need it for safety
bullets.body: Put it in a bag or pocket on Do Not Disturb. Do not use social media, video, news, or the browser.

bullets.head: Cannot walk
bullets.body: Spend 20 minutes in a different shared or outdoor place without using the phone.

done: The task is done when 20 minutes has passed without using the phone for entertainment or scrolling.

title: Learn to Be Bored
summary: Spend 20 minutes on one slow, screen-free activity.
label: TODAY'S TASK
intro: Set a 20-minute timer and do one slow, screen-free activity.

bullets.head: Hands
bullets.body: Cook, draw, clean, repair, build, make tea, play an instrument, or organise something.

bullets.head: Reading
bullets.body: Read a physical book, magazine, printed paper, or notes.

bullets.head: Outside
bullets.body: Walk, stretch, sit in a park, or tend to something outdoors.

bullets.head: Very tired
bullets.body: Lie down or sit quietly without the phone. Rest is allowed.

done: The task is done when the 20-minute timer ends without switching to a screen.

title: Screen Boundaries
summary: Choose one screen-free time or place and follow the rule today.
label: TODAY'S TASK
intro: Pick one place or time that will be screen-free for the next seven days. Follow the rule once today.

bullets.head: Bed
bullets.body: Move the charger outside the bed area.

bullets.head: Bathroom
bullets.body: Choose a fixed shelf, table, bag, or charging place outside the bathroom where the phone stays.

bullets.head: Meals
bullets.body: Put the phone on a shelf, counter, or charging spot away from the table and use that place at the next meal.

bullets.head: First hour awake
bullets.body: Use the alarm, then put the phone back in its charging place until the first planned task is finished.

done: The task is done when you have chosen the exact place where the phone stays and followed that rule once today.

title: Dopamine Detox
summary: Spend one hour without feeds, porn, news, or short-form content.
label: TODAY'S TASK
intro: Spend one hour today without porn, social media, short videos, recommendation feeds, or news.

bullets.head: Set a 60-minute timer and put those apps and sites aside for the hour.
You can still cook, walk, read, talk to someone, listen to music you chose, watch one film or episode you picked in advance, or work on a hobby.
If you need to stay reachable, use Do Not Disturb and allow calls from family, favourites, or emergency contacts.

done: The task is done when the hour has passed without opening the feeds you set aside.

title: Wake Up With Purpose
summary: Prepare tomorrow's first hour before you go to bed.
label: TODAY'S TASK
intro: Prepare tomorrow's first hour tonight so there is less to decide when you wake up.

bullets.head: Alarm
bullets.body: Set the wake time and put the phone across the room or in its charging place.

bullets.head: Before bed
bullets.body: Lay out clothes, pack the bag, put keys where you can see them, and prepare breakfast or water if it helps.

bullets.head: First activity
bullets.body: Put one event in the calendar for the first hour: breakfast, walk, gym, class, library, work, or another fixed task.

bullets.head: Shift work
bullets.body: Use the first hour after your actual wake time, even if that is afternoon or evening.

done: The task is done when the alarm is set, the first activity is on the calendar, and the basic items are ready.

title: Meaning
summary: Spend 30 minutes on a person, project, skill, or responsibility that matters to you.
label: TODAY'S TASK
intro: Spend 30 minutes today on one person, project, skill, or responsibility.

bullets.head: Person
bullets.body: Call, meet, help, or spend 30 minutes together without multitasking.

bullets.head: Project
bullets.body: Open the file or materials and work on it for 30 minutes.

bullets.head: Skill
bullets.body: Practise one skill for 30 minutes.

bullets.head: Responsibility
bullets.body: Do the job someone is waiting on you to do.

done: The task is done when the 30 minutes are up.

title: Why Relationships Matter
summary: Invite someone to do something with a specific day and time.
label: TODAY'S TASK
intro: Invite someone you trust or enjoy spending time with to do something.

bullets.head: Include an activity, a day, and a rough time
bullets.body: "Coffee Saturday afternoon?" "Gym Tuesday at 6?" "Want to eat after class tomorrow?"

bullets.head: Far away
bullets.body: Suggest a call or video call with a day and time.

bullets.head: Keep the message to one or two sentences and send it.

done: The task is done when the invitation has been sent.

title: Loneliness
summary: Spend 30 minutes around other people, or have a 20-minute call if you cannot leave home.
label: TODAY'S TASK
intro: Spend 30 minutes today in a place where other people are present.

bullets.head: School or university
bullets.body: Use a common room, dining hall, library, club, class, or sports session.

bullets.head: Work
bullets.body: Eat in the shared area, take a break with others, or stay for a short conversation.

bullets.head: Living alone
bullets.body: Use a cafe, gym, library, class, place of worship, club, or another regular public setting.

bullets.head: Cannot leave home
bullets.body: Have a 20-minute phone or video conversation instead.

done: The task is done when you have spent 30 minutes around other people, or had a 20-minute phone or video conversation if you cannot leave home.

title: Solitude
summary: Spend 30 minutes alone without using your phone to escape the quiet.
label: TODAY'S TASK
intro: Spend 30 minutes alone on purpose with the phone in another room or out of reach.

bullets.head: Choose one activity before you start
bullets.body: Cook, read, draw, play music, stretch, clean, write by hand, or sit with tea.

bullets.head: Do not use feeds
bullets.body: No porn, social media, short-form video, or endless browsing.

bullets.head: Shared home
bullets.body: You can use a quiet corner or headphones for music, but keep the phone away from your hands.

done: The task is done when the 30 minutes ends and you stayed alone without using the phone as an escape.

title: What Porn Replaces
summary: Spend time with another person today, or make plans to.
label: TODAY'S TASK
intro: Spend some time with another person today, or make plans to.

bullets.head: If you have a partner
bullets.body: Spend 20 minutes together without phones and tell them something you want more of: time together, affection, conversation, a date, or better sexual communication. Sex is not required for the task.

bullets.head: If you are single
bullets.body: Invite someone to coffee, food, a walk, training, a game, or something else. Friendship counts; you do not need to turn this into dating.

bullets.head: If you have been rejected or hurt recently
bullets.body: Contact someone you trust who is not the person you are chasing for reassurance, or arrange to be around other people.

bullets.head: If social contact feels difficult
bullets.body: Send a short message or spend 20 minutes somewhere other people are around.

bullets.head: If the issue is mainly sexual release and you are not lonely
bullets.body: Follow the boundary you chose in Lesson 21.

done: The task is done when the message or invitation has been sent, or you have spent 20 minutes with another person.

title: Friendship
summary: Turn one casual connection into a second meeting, call, or group session.
label: TODAY'S TASK
intro: Contact someone you have met or spoken to before and arrange what happens next.

bullets.head: Someone you met recently
bullets.body: Invite them to something and include a day and time.

bullets.head: Club, class, sport, or group
bullets.body: Register for or attend the next session and put it in the calendar.

bullets.head: Classmate or colleague
bullets.body: Ask to eat, study, train, or work together and suggest a time.

bullets.head: Existing friend you rarely see
bullets.body: Set a recurring or next meeting instead of saying "we should catch up sometime."

done: The task is done when a second meeting, call, or group session has been arranged or attended.

title: Unhealthy Relationships
summary: Change one relationship, chat, or account that regularly leaves you worse.
label: TODAY'S TASK
intro: Think of one person, group chat, or account that regularly leaves you tense, upset, pressured, or more likely to use porn. Change one thing about how you deal with it today.

bullets.head: Late-night contact
bullets.body: Decide the time after which you stop answering non-urgent calls or messages, and tell the person if they need to know.

bullets.head: A group chat or account that repeatedly humiliates, pressures, or drags you toward behaviour you are leaving
bullets.body: Mute it, leave it, or stop opening it for the next seven days.

bullets.head: A subject someone repeatedly pushes after you have said no
bullets.body: Send one plain sentence such as "I do not want to discuss that."

bullets.head: Invitations you repeatedly regret accepting
bullets.body: Decline the next one now if it is already on the calendar.

bullets.head: No relationship fits
bullets.body: Do not invent one for the lesson. Make plans with someone you like being around instead.

done: The task is done when you have made the change. If no unhealthy relationship fits, it is done when you have made plans with someone.
extra: If you are afraid of someone's reaction, the relationship is controlling, or there is abuse or a threat of violence, do not confront them alone. Involve someone you trust or a qualified professional and put your safety first.

title: Healthy Relationships
summary: Do something today for a relationship you care about.
label: TODAY'S TASK
intro: Do something for a relationship you care about today.

bullets.head: Call
bullets.body: Have a 10-minute conversation without doing something else at the same time.

bullets.head: Plan
bullets.body: Arrange a meal, coffee, walk, game, or visit.

bullets.head: Help
bullets.body: Do something the other person needs.

bullets.head: Repair
bullets.body: If you owe a simple apology or reply, send it today.

done: The task is done when the call, plan, help, or apology is finished.

title: Trauma
summary: Write about a past experience that still affects you and how you want to handle it next time.
label: TODAY'S TASK
intro: Write briefly about a past experience you already know still affects you, what happens when it comes up now, what you usually do to get away from it, and what you could do next time.

bullets.head: Past
bullets.body: Write about the experience only if one already comes to mind. If not, note that you do not know of a trauma link here.

bullets.head: Now
bullets.body: Write what happens when it comes up, such as tension, panic, numbness, shame, withdrawing, avoiding intimacy, or another reaction you recognise.

bullets.head: Escape
bullets.body: Write what you usually do to get away from the feeling or memory. Porn can be one answer, but so can scrolling, drinking, isolating, overworking, or shutting down.

bullets.head: Next time
bullets.body: Write what you could do instead, such as leaving an unsafe setting, grounding yourself in the room, calling a trusted person, writing down what is happening, or contacting a professional.

done: The task is done when you have written about all four parts and prepared anything you may need next time.
extra: Prepare for that situation today. Save the contact, book the appointment, write down grounding steps, or tell the trusted person you may reach out. If you do not know of a trauma link, leave it there; do not invent one.

title: Your Environment
summary: Change one person, account, place, or routine that regularly leaves you more upset or more likely to use porn.
label: TODAY'S TASK
intro: Change one person, account, place, or routine that regularly leaves you more upset, tense, or more likely to use porn.

bullets.head: App or account
bullets.body: Mute, unfollow, log out, or delete it.

bullets.head: Group chat or online community
bullets.body: Mute it for a week, or leave if you no longer use it.

bullets.head: Place or routine
bullets.body: Change the place, time, or phone habit that repeatedly leaves you distressed or more likely to use porn.

bullets.head: Relationship
bullets.body: Reduce contact or decide what you will no longer accept. If the relationship feels unsafe, involve someone you trust rather than confronting the person alone.

done: The task is done when you have changed how often you see the person, open the account, go to the place, or follow the routine.

title: Self-Criticism
summary: Replace one harsh judgment about yourself with the facts and one repair you can start now.
label: TODAY'S TASK
intro: Write down one harsh sentence you have said to yourself recently. Then separate what happened from what you can still fix.

bullets.head: What happened
bullets.body: Write the event without insulting yourself: missed the deadline, relapsed last night, skipped training, forgot the appointment, or whatever is true.

bullets.head: What can still be fixed
bullets.body: Name one repair: send the email, move the phone, book the next session, clean the mess, apologise, or reschedule.

bullets.head: Next 10 minutes
bullets.body: Write the first action and start it now.

done: The task is done when the facts and the repair are written and the first action has started.

title: Self-Loathing
summary: Replace one insult about yourself with facts, then do one basic thing for yourself.
label: TODAY'S TASK
intro: Write down one insult you use about yourself. Then replace it with three facts about what happened.

bullets.head: Keep the facts narrow
bullets.body: what you did, when it happened, and what the consequence was.

bullets.head: Do not replace the insult with praise. You are only making the sentence accurate.
After writing the facts, do something basic for yourself
bullets.body: eat, shower, go outside, clean one surface, take medication you normally take, or go to bed on time.

done: The task is done when the insult has been replaced by facts and you have done the basic thing you chose.

title: Self-Compassion
summary: Look at one recent mistake without insults and start the next useful action.
label: TODAY'S TASK
intro: Choose one recent mistake. Write briefly about what happened, what made the situation harder, and what you will do next. Then do that next action today.

bullets.head: What happened
bullets.body: One sentence, no insults.

bullets.head: What made it harder
bullets.body: Tiredness, stress, alcohol, being alone, a deadline, an argument, a risky feed, or whatever mattered.

bullets.head: What happens next
bullets.body: Write one action you can start in 10 minutes or less.

done: The task is done when the three points are written and the next action has started.

title: Self-Trust
summary: Make one small promise you can keep before bed, then keep it.
label: TODAY'S TASK
intro: Choose one thing you can finish before bed and commit to doing it. Set a reminder now, then do what you said you would do.

bullets.head: Low effort
bullets.body: 10-minute walk, shower, one email, phone outside the bed, or one load of laundry.

bullets.head: Work or study
bullets.body: Work on one task for 20 minutes with the phone away.

bullets.head: Health
bullets.body: Cook one meal, do one short workout, or go to bed at the time you set.

bullets.head: Make it smaller if needed. At bedtime, it should be obvious whether you did it or not.

done: The task is done when the promised action is finished before bed.

title: Self-Improvement
summary: Spend 20 minutes practising a skill instead of watching advice about it.
label: TODAY'S TASK
intro: Set a 20-minute timer and practise one skill. Do not watch self-improvement or motivation content during the timer.

bullets.head: Coding or writing
bullets.body: Produce code, a paragraph, an outline, or an edited page.

bullets.head: Music or art
bullets.body: Practise a chord, passage, technique, drawing, or small piece.

bullets.head: Sport or fitness
bullets.body: Practise one movement, drill, or short session.

bullets.head: Practical skill
bullets.body: Cook, repair, organise, learn some vocabulary, or practise another skill.

done: The task is done after 20 minutes of practice. Watching advice about the skill does not count.

title: Know Yourself
summary: Identify when you are most likely to relapse, what has helped before, and one change to make today.
label: TODAY'S TASK
intro: Open Notes and answer three questions from your own experience. Then act on the last answer today.

bullets.head: When are you most likely to relapse? Write the time, place, device, or situation.
What has helped in that situation before? For example
bullets.body: phone away from bed, a shared space, earlier sleep, plans with someone, or Vici Urge Surfing one tap away.

bullets.head: What will you change today? Pick one change you can make now.
Do it
bullets.body: Move the charger, add the Vici shortcut or widget, change where you use the phone, or put the activity on your calendar.

done: The task is done when all three questions are answered and you have made the change you chose.

title: Amor Fati
summary: Write about something in the past you cannot change and act on what is still possible now.
label: TODAY'S TASK
intro: Choose something from the past you still wish had happened differently. Write briefly about two things:

bullets.head: What has already happened and cannot be changed, such as years spent on porn, a relapse, a breakup, a missed opportunity, lost money, or another past event.

What you can still do now, such as apologising, repaying something, making a booking, applying, deleting an old porn account or saved link, contacting someone, finishing a piece of work, or not repeating the same behaviour tonight.

done: The task is done when you have written about both parts and started the action that is still possible.
extra: Spend 15 minutes on the action that is still possible, or finish it immediately if it is a message, booking, or payment.

title: Memento Mori
summary: Put one hour on the calendar for something porn or empty screen time has been taking time from.
label: TODAY'S TASK
intro: Pick something porn or empty screen time has been taking time from. Put one hour on the calendar for it within the next seven days, and do the first 10 minutes today.

bullets.head: Person
bullets.body: Set the meal, call, visit, date, or time together and send the message now.

bullets.head: Health
bullets.body: Put the session on the calendar and start the first 10 minutes today.

bullets.head: Work or project
bullets.body: Block the hour and do the first 10 minutes now.

bullets.head: Experience or hobby
bullets.body: Choose the date, register or book it if needed, and spend 10 minutes starting today.

done: The task is done when the hour is on the calendar and you have started.

title: Carpe Diem
summary: Spend 20 minutes doing something you keep saying you want to do more often.
label: TODAY'S TASK
intro: Spend 20 minutes today doing something you keep saying you want to do more often.

Play the instrument, train, draw, write, cook, walk somewhere you like, call someone, begin the project, or change something about how you usually end up watching porn. If it needs a booking or another person, make the arrangement and use the remaining time on whatever you can start alone.
If porn has been taking time from this, use some of that time now.
done: The task is done when you have spent 20 minutes on it or put a date in the calendar.

title: The Next 90 Days
summary: Choose one 90-day goal, schedule the weekly work, and start for 20 minutes today.
label: TODAY'S TASK
intro: Pick one goal for the next 90 days. Put the weekly work on your calendar, then do 20 minutes now.

bullets.head: Pick a result you can tell whether you reached
bullets.body: finish a project, train three times a week, submit an application, pass a course, build a portfolio, or something similar.

bullets.head: Decide what you will do each week
bullets.body: two study blocks, three workouts, one application session, one project block, or another repeated action.

bullets.head: Put the repeated time on the calendar for the next four weeks.

done: The task is done when you have written the 90-day goal, put the weekly times on the calendar, and finished today's 20 minutes.

title: Peace of Mind
summary: Spend 30 minutes tonight without incoming content.
label: TODAY'S TASK
intro: Choose a 30-minute part of tonight when you would usually be on a screen or listening to something. Spend it without messages, feeds, news, videos, podcasts, porn, or email.
You can cook, shower, walk, stretch, read a physical book, talk to someone, write, or sit quietly. If you need to stay reachable, allow important calls.
If the quiet feels boring, leave it boring for the half hour instead of opening another feed, video, message thread, podcast, or porn.
done: The task is done when the 30 minutes have passed without replacing one feed with another.

title: This Time Next Year
summary: Schedule the next four times you will do one thing you want in your life a year from now.
label: TODAY'S TASK
intro: Look at the ordinary Tuesday you pictured in the lesson. Pick one part you want to happen regularly and schedule the next four times now.

bullets.head: Relationship
bullets.body: Four weekly meals, calls, walks, or time together.

bullets.head: Health
bullets.body: Four training sessions, classes, runs, or other planned activity.

bullets.head: Work or study
bullets.body: Four blocks for a project or subject you want to keep working on.

bullets.head: Hobby or community
bullets.body: Four sessions, meetings, practices, or events.

done: The task is done when all four dates are in the calendar and the first one is ready to happen.
extra: Put all four dates in the calendar and make any first message or booking needed for the first one.

title: What Forever Means
summary: Choose one rule from the course to keep for the next 90 days and start it today.
label: TODAY'S TASK
intro: Pick one rule from the course that you will keep for the next 90 days. Start it today.

bullets.head: Phone
bullets.body: Keep it out of bed or the bathroom.

bullets.head: Vici
bullets.body: Keep Urge Surfing one tap away on the Home Screen or Lock Screen.

bullets.head: Charger
bullets.body: Keep it in the place you chose during the course, away from the bed or bathroom.

bullets.head: Weekly routine
bullets.body: Keep one regular social, exercise, study, or outside activity.

bullets.head: Add a calendar event 90 days from today to decide whether you want to keep the rule.

done: The task is done when you have followed the rule once and the review date is on your calendar.

title: Twelve Weeks Ago
summary: Compare Week 1 with today in six parts of your life and recovery.
label: TODAY'S TASK
intro: Open Notes. Compare Week 1 with today in six areas.

bullets.head: Phone
bullets.body: Where did it sleep then? Where does it usually sleep now?

bullets.head: Sleep
bullets.body: What did late nights usually look like then? What do they look like now?

bullets.head: Urges
bullets.body: What did you usually do when one started then? What do you do now?

bullets.head: Isolation
bullets.body: How much time did you spend alone in risky places then? What changed?

bullets.head: Time
bullets.body: What now receives time that porn or thinking about recovery used to take?

bullets.head: After a relapse or close call
bullets.body: What happened next then? What would you do now?

done: The task is done when all six comparisons say what you did then and what you do now. Answers such as 'better' or 'worse' are not enough.

title: What Changed in Your Brain
summary: Practise one recovery action that has become easier three times today.
label: TODAY'S TASK
intro: Pick one thing from the course that you now do more easily. Practise it three times today.

bullets.head: Leaving the room
bullets.body: Put the phone down, stand up, leave, then return.

bullets.head: Phone placement
bullets.body: Move the phone to its charging place, return to the bed or desk without it, then repeat.

bullets.head: Leaving a risky room
bullets.body: Walk from that room to the public or shared place you chose, then return.

bullets.head: Vici
bullets.body: Open Urge Surfing from the Home Screen or Lock Screen shortcut, reach the first exercise screen, then exit.

done: The task is done when you have repeated the same action three times from start to finish.

title: Winning the Battle
summary: Use the three things that helped you most during the course.
label: TODAY'S TASK
intro: Pick the three things that helped you most during the course and use all three today.

bullets.head: Vici
bullets.body: Keep Urge Surfing where you can reach it fastest.

bullets.head: Phone or laptop
bullets.body: Put it in the place that worked best during the course.

bullets.head: Time or people
bullets.body: Go to bed at the time you planned, spend the risky part of the evening in a shared place, or make plans with someone.

bullets.head: If something else worked better for you, use that. Choose things you can do today.

done: The task is done when you have used all three today.

title: Lessons From Addiction Recovery
summary: Save three people or services you could contact if you start struggling.
label: TODAY'S TASK
intro: Save three people or services you could contact if you were struggling. Keep them together in one note or contact group.

bullets.head: First person
bullets.body: Add someone you would call: friend, family member, partner, mentor, or someone else you trust.

bullets.head: Professional or service
bullets.body: Save a counsellor, clinician, clinic, support group, or another service you would consider using.

bullets.head: Backup
bullets.body: Add a second person or service in case the first is unavailable.

bullets.head: Write one short message you would send if you wanted company or a call. Use your own words, not a script from the course.

done: The task is done when all three contacts or services and the message are saved in one place.

title: Saying Goodbye
summary: Remove anything that still belongs to the old habit, or use the time for something you want to keep.
label: TODAY'S TASK
intro: Look at what is still left from the old habit and use the case that applies to you.

bullets.head: If you still have a porn bookmark, saved file, secondary account, stored login, browser profile, or physical item
bullets.body: Remove one today.

bullets.head: If you already removed all of it
bullets.body: Do not invent another trigger just to complete the task. Write one sentence naming what you removed during the course, then spend 20 minutes using the time or place for something you want to keep: a book, instrument, workout, project, walk, meal, or time with another person.

bullets.head: If a social feed you still use keeps becoming sexual
bullets.body: Remove the accounts, searches, or recommendations causing it. Keep the rest of the service if you still use it.

done: The task is done when you have removed something that remains. If nothing remains, spend 20 minutes on the book, workout, project, walk, meal, or person you chose.

title: The Future
summary: Write and pin a short plan for what you will do if things start slipping again.
label: TODAY'S TASK
intro: Write one final note you can use if things start slipping again. Keep it short.

bullets.head: Warning signs
bullets.body: Write three changes you can notice, such as the phone returning to bed, repeated late nights, isolating in the room, reopening risky feeds, or cancelling plans.

bullets.head: First thing you will do
bullets.body: Write one action, such as putting the phone in its charging place and leaving the room for 20 minutes.

bullets.head: Two rules you are keeping
bullets.body: Write the one or two habits from the course you intend to continue.

bullets.head: Who you will contact
bullets.body: Write the first person or service you would contact if you start relapsing often or feel unable to stop.

done: The task is done when the note is pinned and short enough to read in under a minute.
